> [!abstract] Key idea
> A rounded patch, a partial ground and a small **defected ground structure (DGS)** stretch the bandwidth to nearly 6:1. Over a band this wide the radiation pattern changes a lot, so a wideband design needs different checks.

- This is an **ultra wideband (UWB)** printed monopole, with a stated range of 3.2 to 20 GHz.
- The substrate is **Rogers RO4003C (lossy)**, 0.813 mm thick. The library value of εr = 3.55 is edited to **3.38**, as in [[16. Wideband Monopole Antenna|Section 16]].
- The patch uses the **Elliptical Cylinder** tool, which takes an X radius and a Y radius.
- The 1.795 mm feed line works out to about 52 Ω on this substrate.
- The patch moves up by 3.3 mm to reach the feed, plus a 0.1 mm overlap so they join cleanly with Add.

## 0.2 Defected Ground Structure
- A **DGS** is a shape cut into the ground plane. It changes how current flows there, which adds a little inductance and capacitance to tune the match.
- This design has a small **U-shaped slot** at the top of the ground, right below the feed.
- It's built from an outer brick and an inner brick, offset by the gap G, so the slot keeps the same width all the way round.

> [!tip] Parameters at work
> The slot is positioned using LG. When LG changes, the slot moves with the ground by itself.

- So the simulation starts slightly above the stated 3.2 GHz.

</svg>

- The lecture's far field shows **four lobes at 10 GHz and ten lobes at 20 GHz**.
- As frequency rises, the same antenna is more wavelengths across, so its pattern splits up.

> [!warning] Wideband in S11 doesn't mean one steady pattern
> A low S11 only shows that power enters the antenna. It says nothing about where that power goes. So check the far field at several frequencies across the band, not just one.

## 0.5 Ground Length Sweep
| LG (mm) | Result |
|---|---|
| 7 | Notch moves up, -16 dB |
| 7.667 | Deepest notch, -31 dB |
| 8 | Original design, about -24 dB |
| 8.333 | Notch moves up, -16 dB |
| 9 | S11 rises above -9 dB, which fails |

> [!warning] Judge a wideband antenna by the whole band
> The lecture picks 7.667 mm because it has the deepest notch. For a UWB antenna, the real test is whether S11 stays **below -10 dB across the full band**. Depth at one frequency matters much less.

## 0.6 Three Monopoles Compared
| | Wire (Section 15) | Rectangular (Section 16) | UWB (this section) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Ground** | Full | Partial | Partial with U slot |
| **Band** | Narrow, near 2.33 GHz | 1.86 to 3.97 GHz | 3.47 to 20 GHz |
| **Ratio** | Narrowband | About 2.1:1 | About 5.8:1 |
| **Pattern** | Doughnut | Doughnut at 3 GHz | Many lobes at high frequency |
